newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin meets EU leaders, says relations good.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin meets EU leaders, says relations good.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin, starting a Kremlin meeting with top representatives of the European Union, said on Monday he was pleased with the way Russia's relations with the community were developing.

"I'm very glad that a pretty good dialogue is getting under way between us and the EU and its leadership," Itar-Tass news agency quoted Yeltsin telling Dutch Prime Minister Wim Kok and European Commission President Jacques Santer.
The Netherlands holds the EU's rotating presidency.

Yeltsin, 66, for whom the meeting marks a further stage in his political comeback after eight months of serious illness, said there was now a permanent exchange of views on political, economic and other matters with Brussels.
"We are satisfied that the European Union is developing and that you are getting more integration," Yeltsin added.

Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin and Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov, as well as Oleg Davydov, Moscow's deputy prime minister in charge of foreign economic relations, were also attending the meeting, Tass said.

Interfax news agency quoted Santer as saying he was sure relations between the EU and Russia would continue to develop strongly but that the present level of ties should not be "underestimated". He noted that Russia's trade with the EU was eight to 10 times greater than with the United States.

At a separate meeting with Chernomyrdin earlier on Monday, Tass said the EU delegation discussed a still unratified accord designed to forge links between the two sides and liberalise trade, other trade matters and the issue of NATO's plans to accept new members in eastern Europe.
